title: GH#39006: fix(recovery): pending --count leaves the supervisor cursor before the first counted entry
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39006

`_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` runs `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending --count` just before it writes the `blocker_recovery` trigger. The count shared `pending_cursor` with the supervisor's own `pending` pass and saved the cursor past every entry it checked. The supervisor's pass then started after exactly the entries that justified the run, and those entries waited a full queue wrap. Every logged trigger count on this runner was a partial scan of 1–7 entries (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`), so most of each run's reachable work was the part the count had already passed.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
  - In `--count` mode, each tier's cursor still advances past non-actionable entries. At the first entry the count would emit, the cursor goes back to the value just before it, and the cursor stays there for the rest of that tier. The count is still reported in full.
  - New `_tbr_restore_cursor`: an empty value removes the cursor file, which is the same as starting at the beginning of the queue.
  - The per-tier scan moved into `_tbr_pending_scan_tier`, the same pattern as `_tbr_pending_discovery_stages`, so `tbr_pending` stays under the 100-line function limit. `break 3` became `return 3`; a cursor write failure still makes `tbr_pending` return 2.
  - Plain `pending` and `--rearm-only` (`rearm_cursor`) behave exactly as before.
- `TODO.md`: t19103 recorded; t19100 marked done (GH#38990 closed by PR #38992).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, which sources the capability and discovery suites: `Tests run: 62 failed: 0`.
- Ad hoc check that stubs the entry checks over a 5-entry queue (not committed):
  - Count stops the cursor before the first counted entry.
  - Plain `pending` then starts at that entry and still advances.
  - After a wrap, the count restores the pre-wrap cursor.
  - When the first entry is the counted one, the cursor file is removed.
  - A count with nothing actionable advances through the whole queue.
  - All checks pass on this branch. Against `main`, "count stops before first actionable" fails: the cursor ends past the counted entry, which reproduces the defect.

## Risk

Low. The change only affects the `--count` probe's cursor writes. If the supervisor's run never happens (cooldown or failure), the next probe walks the same window again and triggers again, which is the intended retry.

title: GH#39008: fix(pulse): re-probe blocker recovery after a partial zero-count scan instead of waiting the full interval
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39008

`_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` stamps its 3h interval, then runs a budget-bounded `pending --count` walk over part of the recovery queue. When that partial walk found nothing, the next probe still waited the full 3h, so one walk of a ~125-entry queue took about a day. On this runner, in the week to 2026-11-18, `trigger=blocker_recovery` starts had gaps of 51h and 27h, against an interval that allows 8 runs a day. Every logged trigger count was a partial scan.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`
  - New `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe`. After a partial (rc 2) zero-count probe, it writes an absolute deadline (`now + PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_PARTIAL_PROBE_INTERVAL`, default 600s, the rearm cadence) to `last_blocker_recovery_partial_due_epoch`, then logs one line: `blocker recovery probe found 0 pending (partial scan); re-probe in 600s`.
  - The full-interval stamp is not rewritten.
  - The interval is parsed as decimal, so `0600` means 600s.
  - No deadline is written when the partial interval is not below the current interval, or when cached API pressure is active.
  - `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` treats the probe as due when the interval has elapsed or the partial deadline has passed. It still checks the failure cooldown first, and it clears the deadline when a probe starts.
  - The deadline holds even if the interval changes before it is reached, for example a 1800s failure-retry interval followed by a success that restores 10800s.
  - A failed or truncated deadline write reads as 0: no early probe, and the full interval is kept.
  - New `_pulse_blocker_api_pressure_active`: the GraphQL circuit-breaker and secondary-cooldown guard, extracted from `_pulse_rearm_blocker_holds`, which now calls it with the same behaviour.
  - A complete zero-count scan, any positive count, and the failure-retry interval behave as before.

Pairs with #39007 (GH#39006). That PR keeps the count from moving the supervisor's cursor past counted entries; without it, faster probes would skip more entries.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`: `19/19 tests passed`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: `Tests run: 62 failed: 0`, including "mechanical rearm cadence ... respects API cooldown and circuit state".
- An ad hoc stub-helper check of the real `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` (not committed) passed 16/16:
  - partial zero-count: no trigger, stamp unchanged, deadline at +600s, log line written;
  - not due at +599s; the probe runs at +600s and clears the deadline;
  - complete zero-count: no deadline;
  - partial positive count triggers;
  - circuit-breaker state: no deadline;
  - partial interval at or above the current interval: no deadline;
  - `0600` is read as decimal;
  - a deadline written under the 1800s retry interval still fires at +600s after the interval grows to 10800s;
  - a failed deadline write keeps the full interval and logs nothing.

## Risk

Low. While the queue holds nothing actionable, probes run about every 10 minutes, the same GitHub read cost as the existing 10-minute rearm pass. They stop as soon as a probe finds work, because the trigger then takes the normal interval.

title: t19105: fix(recovery): reserve a queue share for decided holds so replies, policy changes and retries can wake them
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39010

`tbr_pending` scans tier 0 (entries without a standing `human_decision`) through a full rotation before tier 1 (decided entries) starts (GH#38692). Both tiers share one queue deadline. On a live runner, tier 0 never finishes inside the ~29s pending window or the 45s rearm window. `pending_cursor_decided` and `rearm_cursor_decided` had never been written, although `_tbr_pending_scan_tier` saves the tier cursor before every entry check.

The effect: every positive wake signal for a decided hold lives in tier 1, and none of them could fire. That covers a maintainer reply newer than the decision (GH#38311), a changed repo recovery policy (t19068), and a trusted retry or brief revision in rearm mode. A maintainer who answered a decision packet got no action. Current example: 14 `human_decision` records in one managed repo carry no policy fingerprint, although that repo now declares a recovery policy; none has been re-assessed.

## Changes

All changes are in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`.

- **`_tbr_pending_classify`** classifies the queue once per run. It uses two batched jq reads (queue identities, then decision wakes), so the process count stays constant: 129 entries take ~40 ms, against ~1.5 s for per-entry reads. An unreadable file falls back to the per-entry check, never to a guessed tier.
- **`_tbr_pending_reserve`** applies when any entry is decided. Tier 0 ends `max(1, remaining / 4)` seconds early once at least 2 seconds remain; a single second goes to tier 0. With no decided entries, tier 0 keeps the whole window.
- **`_tbr_pending_scan_tier`** shadows `TBR_QUEUE_DEADLINE` for tier 0, so identity and entry stages cannot run into tier 1's share.
  - At its deadline, tier 0 logs `reason=budget_exhausted tier=0 (decided-tier share reserved)` and returns 4. The run is marked incomplete only if entries remain unobserved.
  - The queue deadline still stops both tiers (rc 3).
  - Entries already observed this run are skipped.
- **Tier-0 resume.** When tier 1 finishes early, tier 0 resumes in the time left, so the reservation never sits idle. A `--count` probe that already counted a tier-0 entry does not resume; its GH#39006 cursor hold stays in place.
- **`_tbr_pending_park`** handles a tier-0 entry that the reservation itself cut short. It parks the cursor just before the entry and writes a `<cursor>_full_window` marker, and the next run gives tier 0 the whole window. A pending pass clears the marker; a `--count` probe only reads it. Without this, an entry needing more than the tier-0 share would time out on every pulse. Worst case, an entry needing more than the whole window alternates between reserved and full-window runs.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: `Tests run: 62 failed: 0`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`: `35 run, 0 failed`.
- Ad hoc reproduction (8s budget, 1s per check, 18 undecided + 2 decided entries). On `main`, the decided tier was never reached and no `*_cursor_decided` file was written. On this branch, a decided entry was checked in rearm mode, both decided cursors were written, and the tier-0 share message was logged. With no decided entries, tier 0 still used the full window.
- Review-fix checks, each passing in 3 consecutive runs:
  - batched/per-entry classification parity, including malformed files;
  - tier-0 stage deadline below tier 1's;
  - identity yield;
  - tier-0 resume with no duplicate checks;
  - 3s window (tier 1 reached) and 1s window (no reservation);
  - three-run parking: cut and parked, full window and completed, rotation moved on.
- GH#39006 count-cursor checks: 7/7.

## After deploy

`pending_cursor_decided` and `rearm_cursor_decided` should appear in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery/` within one pulse cycle. Decided records without a policy fingerprint, in a repo that now has a policy, should then be re-assessed.

title: t19106: fix(pulse): early blocker re-probe rechecks API pressure and follows only queue-side partial scans
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #39009 (GH#39008), from its review on #39011. In two cases the early blocker-recovery re-probe fired when it should not have:

1. **Pressure that starts after the deadline was saved.** `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe` checked cached API pressure only when it saved the early deadline. If pressure started later, the early probe still ran at the deadline. `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` now rechecks pressure when it reaches a saved partial deadline. It keeps the deadline, so the probe runs once pressure clears.
2. **Partial scans caused only by discovery.** `pending --count` returns 2 for any incomplete stage. The bounded seed spans every pulse repo and rarely finishes in one call, so a run that finished its queue pass could still schedule a probe every partial interval. The probe's stderr is now saved to `last_blocker_recovery_probe.err`. An early probe is scheduled only when the helper reports a queue-side stage as incomplete (`queue`, `identity` or `entry`). Discovery-only partials (`seed`, `holds`, `unclassified`) keep the full interval. Missing or unreadable stderr also means no early probe, the existing safe default.

Resolves #39012

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`: `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe` takes an `err_file` argument and requires a queue-side marker. `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` rechecks pressure at the partial deadline and saves the probe's stderr.
- NEW `todo/tasks/t19106-brief.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`: clean.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`: pass.
- Ad hoc partial-probe checks: pass. Queue-side markers schedule the probe. Discovery-only markers, empty stderr and a missing file do not. Pressure at the deadline defers the probe and keeps the deadline, and it fires once pressure clears.
- Compatible with #39011: its tier-0 yield line (`incomplete stage=queue ... tier=0`) matches the queue-side pattern.

title: t19111: fix(worktree-deps): skip Spotlight marker and tool-cache entries at node_modules root instead of rejecting the restore
body:
## Summary

Dependency provisioning for worker worktrees rejected sources whose `node_modules` root held non-module entries created by macOS or build tools: a Spotlight `.metadata_never_index` marker, `.DS_Store`, and Vite or other tool caches (`.vite`, `.vite-temp`, `.cache`). `resolution_root()` treated each of them as a package root, so `check_package_root()` raised `unrecorded-module-file`. On one managed pnpm repo that accounted for 330 of the last 406 rejections in the pulse log.

- `_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`: a typed allowlist of top-level entries that are skipped: neither counted, copied, recorded nor inventoried, exactly like the existing interrupted pnpm staging skip. Marker names are skipped only as regular files, and cache names only as real directories (lstat, so never symlinks).
- The trust boundary is unchanged. Node resolves bare specifiers such as `require('.extra.js')` to `node_modules/.extra.js`, so any other unrecorded entry, and any allowlisted name with another type, still rejects. A worker cannot resolve a skipped entry, because it is never copied.

Scope, measured: that repo's source `node_modules` is about 3.9 GB, against the 64 MiB copy budget. With this fix it will reject on the byte or entry budget, or on `stale-installed-lock` (the current read-only result) instead. Workers there keep installing from the lockfile per `workflows/full-loop.md`. This PR removes the false rejection for sources that fit the budget. Fast provisioning for large pnpm sources is separate work.

Resolves #39037

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`: 32/32 pass. The new `test_root_markers_and_tool_caches_are_skipped` runs the real restore path for npm and pnpm with all five entries present. It asserts that the package was copied and none of the entries were. It then asserts that a symlinked `.cache` and a directory named `.metadata_never_index` still refuse the restore. The existing `.extra.js` rejection case is unchanged.

title: GH#38959: key OAuth pool seats by email + Anthropic org (Team + Personal on one email)
body:
## Summary

OAuth pool identity is now a seat: email plus optional Anthropic orgId (key `email#orgId`; legacy entries without orgId keep the email-only key). A Team and a Personal grant on the same email become separate seats that rotate independently. New grants take their org from the token response, falling back to the profile endpoint. When an email has one legacy no-org seat, its org is resolved with that seat's own unexpired token (never refreshed); a different org adds a seat ('split'), an unresolved one updates in place with a warning. A grant without org for a multi-seat email is refused and parked as pending. A grant without org that updates a single org-tagged seat keeps that seat's org. Same-email CRUD (remove, set-priority, assign-pending, remote-sync get/put) takes `--org` (orgId prefix or org name, case-insensitive) and refuses ambiguity instead of acting on the first match. JS covers storage, provider-auth (V1/V2), proxy retry/cooldowns, rotation probe and display; Python covers CRUD, rotate, refresh, health and entry-sync; shell covers add/manage/remote-sync/diagnose. title: t19115: fix(checkpoints): a trusted terminal-blocker re-arm releases a blocked worker draft
body:
## Summary

Terminal-blocker recovery re-arms a held issue for a maintainer retry (trusted_retry) or a revision after the blocker (revision_changed) and projects status:available. When the blocked worker left a draft, the draft still held the issue until someone copied a revision-bound approval line, so even a maintainer retry directive was ignored. A census of open blocked-checkpoint drafts found 4 of 9 already re-armed with refusal=none and no approval; one had waited more than 50 hours. `_pcc_policy_route` now calls the new `_pcc_rearmed_checkpoint_route` before the unknown-triage route. It publishes the existing approval line once per receipt when: the newest unedited receipt after the blocked release is trusted_retry or revision_changed; the receipt poster, publisher and runner have write permission; trusted_retry also has an unedited OWNER/MEMBER retry directive from a write-authorised login between the release and the receipt; revision_changed has a write-authorised issue author (only the author or a write collaborator can edit the body); the issue is open, unassigned, auto-dispatchable and unheld; the draft is eligible; and the template binds the current head and brief SHA. A native ref `refs/aidevops/checkpoint-rearm/ISSUE/RECEIPT` makes publication at-most-once across runners. Permission-window and lifecycle re-arms never qualify. Repos opt out with `checkpoint_policy.auto_continue_rearmed: false`. `dispatch-approved` keeps every continuation gate. The motivating draft is a revision_changed case, and the re-arm already treats that revision as release-worthy for ordinary dispatch. The brief update is in planning PR #39079. title: t19116: perf(pulse): take the dispatch launch slot at the claim so rejections evaluate in parallel
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39087

`_dispatch_max_loop` reserved a worker slot for every in-flight ceremony, and the ceremony cap was clamped to the free-slot count. Most candidates are rejected by read-only dedup layers long before the first persistent write. On a busy runner with few free slots, rejections were therefore evaluated one at a time while 80–110 candidates waited. The evidence is in the issue: average occupancy was about 6–7 workers against a target of 20, 22% of capacity samples had zero workers, and one cycle ran 37 candidates strictly in sequence.

This PR moves the reservation to the claim point:

- **Launch-slot semaphore** (`pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`). `_dispatch_max_loop` owns a private slot directory (budget = `effective_slots`). `_dispatch_launch_slot_acquire` takes `slot.N` atomically with `mkdir`. `_dispatch_launch_slot_settle` keeps the slot on rc 0 (launched) or rc 124 (state unknown after the timeout kill) and releases it on any other rc. A success that bypassed the claim point takes an overflow slot, and acquire backs off when overflow would exceed the budget. Without a loop-owned directory (serial loop, direct callers), acquire always succeeds and behaviour does not change.
- **Claim-point acquire** (`pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`). `_dlw_claim_slot_and_lock` takes the slot immediately before `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`, which is the first persistent claim write. If every slot is held, it returns rc 75 (`_DISPATCH_CYCLE_BUDGET_DEFER_RC`). That rc's existing path records a deferral and clears the attempt-recency stamp. It writes no claim and records no fast-fail, backoff or negative cache. The outcome line reads `reason=launch_slot_full`.
- **Evaluation concurrency** (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`). `_dispatch_eval_parallel_cap` returns `slots × DISPATCH_EVAL_OVERSUBSCRIBE` (default 3) and replaces the bare slot clamp in `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase`, so 1- and 2-slot rounds no longer drop to serial. `DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL` (default 6), the throttle file, a forced floor and REST-core serial mode keep their caps. `_dispatch_max_await_slot` waits for a free launch slot instead of a ceremony reservation. It ends the round when every slot is held and nothing is in flight.
- **Opt-out**: `DISPATCH_LAUNCH_SLOT_GATE=0` restores the ceremony-start reservation and the slot clamp exactly. This is documented in `.agents/reference/configuration.md`.

Scope note: the brief named `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` for the helpers. They live in `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, beside the other capacity helpers, and the claim wrapper lives in `pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`, beside `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`: 90/90 pass. New cases:
  - A 1-slot round evaluates candidates concurrently (peak ≥ 2), launches exactly one and defers the rest with `rc=75|reason=launch_slot_full`, with zero failures.
  - A holder whose claim fails releases its slot, and a later candidate launches.
  - `_dlw_claim_slot_and_lock` contract: it defers without a claim, claims when a slot is free, returns 2 on a claim failure (slot released), and treats overflow as consumed budget.
  - The 4-slot budget holds with the gate on and off. The parallel cap oversubscribes ×3, and the legacy and forced-floor modes keep the slot cap.
  - Priority-loop stubs now pass the claim point like production launches.
- These suites pass unchanged: `test-dispatch-min-concurrency`, `test-runner-capability`, `test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing`, `test-prelaunch-publication-reserve`, `test-pulse-dispatch-core-pr-target-guard`, `test-status-label-state-machine`, `test-precreation-failure-skip`, `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave`, `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot`, `test-pulse-dispatch-stage-rc-adapter`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection`.
- ShellCheck is clean on all changed scripts. markdownlint is clean. The pre-commit ratchets pass.

## Post-deploy check

`rg 'loop body finished' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail` should show `mode=parallel(N)` with N above the free-slot count in low-slot rounds, and `launch_slot_full` deferrals should stay a small fraction of the candidates processed. Over 12 hours, the occupancy census (`worker-occupancy.sh`) should show the average concurrent workers rising from the ~6–7 baseline.

title: GH#39095: fix(model-availability): treat a usable OAuth pool account as provider auth on OpenCode 2
body:
Resolves #39095

## Problem

On OpenCode 2.x the model availability probe reports every provider as `no-key`, so `resolve standard` / `resolve thinking` fail and Pulse never dispatches a worker. `resolve_api_key` only reads `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` for OAuth, and OpenCode 2 keeps credentials in its own database and does not write that file. The aidevops OAuth pool (`~/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json`) was only used to *block* a provider (cooldown / all-auth-error), never as a positive credential signal.

## Change

`.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`

- Adds Source 5 to `resolve_api_key`: when the OAuth pool holds at least one account for the provider that is neither `auth-error` nor inside an active `rate-limited` cooldown, return the existing `oauth-refresh-available` marker with `RESOLVED_API_KEY_SOURCE=oauth-pool:<provider>`. This reuses the Source 4 OAuth path (record healthy, skip the HTTP probe), so no probe-lib changes are needed.
- New read-only helper `_resolve_oauth_pool_available` (honours `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE`, same selection rules as `_probe_oauth_pool_cooldown_gate`, never prints credential material).
- Sources 1-4 keep priority, so env/gopass/credentials/auth.json behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

On macOS, OpenCode v2.3.0, one healthy Anthropic pool account, no `auth.json`:

- Before: `probe anthropic --force` → `no API key configured`; `resolve standard` → `No available model for tier: standard`.
- After: `probe anthropic --force` → `OAuth refresh token available`, `1 healthy`; `resolve standard` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`; `resolve thinking` → `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.
- Negative: `probe openai --force` (no pool accounts) → still `1 no key`; `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE=/nonexistent probe anthropic --force` → still `1 no key`.
- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh` clean; pre-commit validation passed.

## Summary

Unsafe or unresolvable paths fall back to `sudo aidevops`. All approval-command printing sites (approval helper help/commands/permissions, worker-permission-helper, pulse NMR/merge-gates/diagnose/reconcile/dependabot/triage, full-loop merge/readiness, dispatch policy, quality-feedback, Cloudron release approval, pulse-check report) now use the renderer. title: t19122: perf(pulse): let a running dispatch round absorb worker slots freed mid-round
body:
## Summary

A parallel max-path round sizes its slot budget once, then runs for tens of minutes; worker exits during the round record the event-refill trigger, but the refill cannot take the instance lock the round holds (lock_busy), so freed slots idled until the next round. When the worker-exit trigger is newer than the round's last capacity read, a spent budget now re-reads _dispatch_compute_capacity and rises to launched + free - hold (pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh _dispatch_round_topup_due/_dispatch_round_topup_budget; launch-slot budget file replaced atomically). _dispatch_max_loop/_dispatch_max_await_slot adopt the raised budget; _dispatch_priority_loop tops up at each drained phase boundary; serial reserved pools hold the other pool's share; concurrent pools, floor, throttle and serial rounds never top up. dispatch_max stamps its capacity read through _dispatch_round_capacity_read (function size unchanged at the 100-line gate). Documented in reference/configuration.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/configuration.md, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

Re-read capacity only when the worker-exit trigger mtime is at or after the last read, so idle rounds make no extra process scans. Target counts recorded launches; in-flight launch-slot holders are still subtracted by the existing slot checks, so the cap stays conservative. Concurrent priority pools are excluded because both would claim the same freed slots; the next phase boundary absorbs them. Opt-out DISPATCH_ROUND_TOPUP=0; DISPATCH_ROUND_TOPUP_MAX_ROUND_S (default 1800) ends absorption in long rounds so a fresh census runs. Production occupancy impact is unmeasured until deployed.

title: GH#39167: guard worker PR base branch (explicit base, stacked-parent validation, retarget fallbacks)
body:
## Summary

Adds shared-pr-base.sh, one PR-base resolver (dispatch env > .aidevops.json > repos.json pr_base_branch > GitHub default > origin/HEAD; never a hard-coded main). commit-and-pr now always passes an explicit --base and logs its source; --base must be the PR base or an open parent PR head (workers fail closed, interactive warns). Stacked children are retargeted to the merged parent's own baseRefName instead of a main fallback (pulse + interactive). The pulse merge pass retargets a worker PR on a wrong non-parent base when its head is built on the PR base, otherwise posts one diagnosis and holds, before conflict/CI-repair routing. Orphan recovery delegates to the shared resolver and refuses to guess main.
